from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Setup layout
        title_text = "The Intuition: Different Maps, Same World"
        lecture_lines = [
            "A point's location is absolute, but its coordinates vary.",
            "Different observers use different grids to describe space.",
            "Alice sees standard tiles; Bob sees a skewed rug."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title_text, lecture_lines)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Create Alice's grid first to use its coordinate system for the absolute point
        alice_grid = NumberPlane(
            x_range=[-4, 4, 1],
            y_range=[-4, 4, 1],
            background_line_style={"stroke_color": "#ADD8E6", "stroke_width": 1, "stroke_opacity": 0.4},
            axis_config={"stroke_color": "#ADD8E6", "stroke_width": 2}
        )
        # Position but don't add yet
        self.place_in_area(alice_grid, 'A1', 'F6', scale_factor=0.6)
        
        # The 'cat' is at a fixed position in space
        # We'll place it at (2, 1) in Alice's system
        cat_pos = alice_grid.coords_to_point(2, 1)
        cat_dot = Dot(point=cat_pos, color=WHITE, radius=0.1)
        
        # Yellow glow for emphasis
        glow = Circle(radius=0.18, color=YELLOW, stroke_width=4).set_opacity(0.6)
        glow.move_to(cat_pos)
        
        # Highlight line 1 and show the absolute point
        self.play(
            self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(YELLOW),
            FadeIn(cat_dot),
            Create(glow),
            run_time=1.5
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Highlight line 2 - simple focus shift
        self.play(
            self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(YELLOW),
            run_time=1
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Alice's Label
        alice_label = Text("Alice (Standard)", font_size=24, color="#ADD8E6")
        self.place_at_grid(alice_label, 'A1', scale_factor=0.6)
        
        # Bob's grid setup (skewed)
        bob_grid = NumberPlane(
            x_range=[-4, 4, 1],
            y_range=[-4, 4, 1],
            background_line_style={"stroke_color": "#90EE90", "stroke_width": 1, "stroke_opacity": 0.4},
            axis_config={"stroke_color": "#90EE90", "stroke_width": 2}
        )
        # Apply shear matrix for a distinct visual difference
        matrix = [[1, 0.4, 0], [0.2, 1, 0], [0, 0, 1]]
        bob_grid.apply_matrix(matrix)
        self.place_in_area(bob_grid, 'A1', 'F6', scale_factor=0.6)
        
        bob_label = Text("Bob (Basis B)", font_size=24, color="#90EE90")
        self.place_at_grid(bob_label, 'A1', scale_factor=0.6)

        # Show Alice's grid
        self.play(
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#ADD8E6"),
            FadeIn(alice_grid),
            FadeIn(alice_label),
            run_time=1.5
        )
        self.wait(2)
        
        # Transition to Bob's grid
        # The cat_dot remains stationary to emphasize absolute position
        self.play(
            self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#90EE90"),
            FadeOut(alice_grid),
            FadeOut(alice_label),
            FadeIn(bob_grid),
            FadeIn(bob_label),
            run_time=1.5
        )
        self.wait(2)
        
        # Return lecture line to white to conclude the section
        self.play(
            self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            run_time=1
        )
        self.wait(2)

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Setup layout with title and lecture lines from storyboard
        self.setup_layout("Prerequisite Review: Basis and Coordinates", [
            "A basis consists of linearly independent spanning vectors.",
            "Any vector is a recipe of these basis elements.",
            "Standard basis vectors i and j form our grid."
        ])
        
        # Colors defined in storyboard and for visual clarity
        color_i = "#FF0000"
        color_j = "#00FF00"
        color_vec = "#FFFF00"
        color_label = "#FFFFFF"

        # Define key grid points
        origin = self.grid["E2"]
        i_end = self.grid["E3"]
        j_end = self.grid["D2"]
        
        # Create standard basis vectors
        i_hat = Arrow(start=origin, end=i_end, buff=0, color=color_i)
        j_hat = Arrow(start=origin, end=j_end, buff=0, color=color_j)
        
        # Labels for basis vectors
        i_label = MathTex(r"\hat{i}", color=color_i, font_size=24)
        j_label = MathTex(r"\hat{j}", color=color_j, font_size=24)
        
        # Positioning labels within 1 grid unit
        i_label.next_to(i_hat, DOWN, buff=0.1)
        j_label.next_to(j_hat, LEFT, buff=0.1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Highlight first lecture line and show basis vectors
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        self.play(Create(i_hat), Create(j_hat))
        self.play(Write(i_label), Write(j_label))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Highlight second lecture line and show vector addition steps
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE), self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        
        # Grid background for the recipe area (E2 to C5)
        grid_bkg = VGroup()
        for col_idx in range(2, 6): # Columns 2, 3, 4, 5
            grid_bkg.add(Line(self.grid[f"E{col_idx}"], self.grid[f"C{col_idx}"], color=GRAY, stroke_width=1, stroke_opacity=0.3))
        for row_char in ["E", "D", "C"]:
            grid_bkg.add(Line(self.grid[f"{row_char}2"], self.grid[f"{row_char}5"], color=GRAY, stroke_width=1, stroke_opacity=0.3))
        
        self.play(FadeIn(grid_bkg))

        # Recipe vectors: 3*i + 2*j
        # i steps
        r_i1 = Arrow(start=origin, end=self.grid["E3"], buff=0, color=color_i, stroke_width=2)
        r_i2 = Arrow(start=self.grid["E3"], end=self.grid["E4"], buff=0, color=color_i, stroke_width=2)
        r_i3 = Arrow(start=self.grid["E4"], end=self.grid["E5"], buff=0, color=color_i, stroke_width=2)
        
        # j steps
        r_j1 = Arrow(start=self.grid["E5"], end=self.grid["D5"], buff=0, color=color_j, stroke_width=2)
        r_j2 = Arrow(start=self.grid["D5"], end=self.grid["C5"], buff=0, color=color_j, stroke_width=2)

        self.play(Create(r_i1), Create(r_i2), Create(r_i3), run_time=2)
        self.play(Create(r_j1), Create(r_j2), run_time=1.5)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Highlight third lecture line and show final vector with label
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(WHITE), self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        
        # Resulting vector [3, 2]
        vec_32 = Arrow(start=origin, end=self.grid["C5"], buff=0, color=color_vec, stroke_width=6)
        vec_label = MathTex(r"\begin{bmatrix} 3 \\ 2 \end{bmatrix}", color=color_label, font_size=32)
        vec_label.next_to(self.grid["C5"], UR, buff=0.1)

        self.play(Create(vec_32))
        self.play(Write(vec_label))
        self.wait(2)
        
        # Reset lecture highlights
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(WHITE))
        self.wait(1)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Setup layout
        self.setup_layout(
            "The 'New' Ruler: Defining Basis B", 
            [
                "Basis B introduces a new set of coordinate axes.",
                "Vectors u and v point in non-standard directions.",
                "This creates a skewed grid over the standard system."
            ]
        )
        
        # Define base colors
        STANDARD_GREY = "#555555"
        VECTOR_U_COLOR = "#FFA500"  # Bright orange
        VECTOR_V_COLOR = "#800080"  # Bright purple
        HIGHLIGHT_COLOR = YELLOW

        # Create Standard Grid
        # Range adjusted to fit well within the A1-F6 area
        std_grid = NumberPlane(
            x_range=[-3, 3, 1],
            y_range=[-3, 3, 1],
            background_line_style={
                "stroke_color": STANDARD_GREY,
                "stroke_width": 2,
                "stroke_opacity": 0.6
            },
            axis_config={"stroke_color": STANDARD_GREY}
        )
        # Place standard grid in the visual area
        self.place_in_area(std_grid, "A1", "F6", scale_factor=0.8)
        origin_pos = std_grid.c2p(0, 0)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Highlight lecture line 1
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(HIGHLIGHT_COLOR))
        self.play(FadeIn(std_grid))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Define vectors u and v relative to std_grid
        u_vec = Arrow(
            start=origin_pos, 
            end=std_grid.c2p(1, 1), 
            buff=0, 
            color=VECTOR_U_COLOR,
            stroke_width=6
        )
        v_vec = Arrow(
            start=origin_pos, 
            end=std_grid.c2p(-1, 1), 
            buff=0, 
            color=VECTOR_V_COLOR,
            stroke_width=6
        )
        
        # Labels for vectors
        # Using Text with slant=ITALIC to bypass potential LaTeX installation issues causing RuntimeError
        u_label = Text("u", slant=ITALIC, color=VECTOR_U_COLOR, font_size=32).next_to(u_vec.get_end(), UR, buff=0.1)
        v_label = Text("v", slant=ITALIC, color=VECTOR_V_COLOR, font_size=32).next_to(v_vec.get_end(), UL, buff=0.1)

        # Update lecture line colors
        self.play(
            self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(VECTOR_U_COLOR)
        )
        
        self.play(Create(u_vec), Write(u_label))
        self.play(Create(v_vec), Write(v_label))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Create skewed grid lines (parallels to u and v)
        skewed_lines_u = VGroup() 
        skewed_lines_v = VGroup() 
        
        # Grid range from -3 to 3 for basis coordinates
        for i in range(-3, 4):
            # Lines parallel to v, shifted along u
            start_v = std_grid.c2p(i - 3, i + 3)
            end_v = std_grid.c2p(i + 3, i - 3)
            line_v = Line(start_v, end_v, color=VECTOR_V_COLOR, stroke_width=1, stroke_opacity=0.4)
            skewed_lines_v.add(line_v)
            
            # Lines parallel to u, shifted along v
            start_u = std_grid.c2p(-3 - i, -3 + i)
            end_u = std_grid.c2p(3 - i, 3 + i)
            line_u = Line(start_u, end_u, color=VECTOR_U_COLOR, stroke_width=1, stroke_opacity=0.4)
            skewed_lines_u.add(line_u)

        skewed_grid = VGroup(skewed_lines_u, skewed_lines_v)
        
        # Origin point flash
        origin_dot = Dot(origin_pos, color=WHITE, radius=0.08)

        self.play(
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(HIGHLIGHT_COLOR)
        )
        
        self.play(Create(skewed_grid))
        self.play(Flash(origin_dot, color=WHITE, line_length=0.3, flash_radius=0.2, num_lines=12))
        self.add(origin_dot)
        self.wait(2)

        # Final cleanup highlight
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(WHITE))
        self.wait(1)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Setup the layout with the lecture lines and title
        lecture_lines = [
            "Matrix P translates coordinates between different basis systems.",
            "It converts Basis B coordinates into the standard system.",
            "Columns of P are Basis B vectors in standard form.",
            "Multiplying Bob's coordinates by P yields Alice's coordinates.",
            "This bridge connects two different ways of seeing space."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("The Bridge: The Change of Basis Matrix", lecture_lines)

        # Colors
        color_col1 = "#FFA500" # Orange
        color_col2 = "#800080" # Purple

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        
        matrix_p_initial = MathTex(
            "P", "=", r"\begin{bmatrix} 1 & -1 \\ 1 & 1 \end{bmatrix}",
            font_size=42, color=WHITE
        )
        self.place_at_grid(matrix_p_initial, "B2", scale_factor=1.0)
        self.play(Write(matrix_p_initial))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(
            self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(YELLOW)
        )
        
        bridge_label = MathTex(r"P: [\vec{v}]_B \mapsto [\vec{v}]_{\text{Standard}}", font_size=32, color=BLUE)
        self.place_at_grid(bridge_label, "A2", scale_factor=0.8)
        self.play(FadeIn(bridge_label))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(YELLOW)
        )
        
        # Fixed logic: Using Matrix class instead of manual partial LaTeX environments
        matrix_elements = [["1", "-1"], ["1", "1"]]
        matrix_p_colored_m = Matrix(
            matrix_elements,
            element_to_mobject_config={"font_size": 42},
            left_bracket="[",
            right_bracket="]"
        )
        # Apply colors to columns
        matrix_p_colored_m.get_columns()[0].set_color(color_col1)
        matrix_p_colored_m.get_columns()[1].set_color(color_col2)
        
        p_label = MathTex("P =", font_size=42).next_to(matrix_p_colored_m, LEFT)
        matrix_p_colored = VGroup(p_label, matrix_p_colored_m)
        
        # Position at the same spot as initial
        self.place_at_grid(matrix_p_colored, "B2", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        self.play(Transform(matrix_p_initial, matrix_p_colored))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.play(
            self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[3].animate.set_color(YELLOW)
        )
        
        # Calculation: P * [1, 1]_B = [0, 2]_Standard
        calc = MathTex(
            r"P \cdot \begin{bmatrix} 1 \\ 1 \end{bmatrix}_B",
            "=",
            r"\begin{bmatrix} 0 \\ 2 \end{bmatrix}_S",
            font_size=36
        )
        self.place_at_grid(calc, "D2", scale_factor=1.0)
        self.play(Write(calc))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.play(
            self.lecture[3].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[4].animate.set_color(YELLOW)
        )
        
        # Center of visual area (roughly D5)
        viz_center = self.grid["D5"]
        
        # Alice's Standard Grid
        std_grid = NumberPlane(
            x_range=[-3, 3, 1], y_range=[-3, 3, 1],
            background_line_style={"stroke_opacity": 0.2},
            axis_config={"stroke_opacity": 0.4}
        ).scale(0.5).move_to(viz_center)
        
        # Bob's Basis B Grid (Transformed by P)
        bob_grid = NumberPlane(
            x_range=[-3, 3, 1], y_range=[-3, 3, 1],
            background_line_style={"stroke_color": BLUE, "stroke_opacity": 0.3},
            axis_config={"stroke_color": BLUE, "stroke_opacity": 0.5}
        ).scale(0.5).apply_matrix([[1, -1], [1, 1]]).move_to(viz_center)
        
        self.play(Create(std_grid))
        self.play(Create(bob_grid))
        
        # Plot the point: [1, 1] in Basis B = [0, 2] in Standard
        point_coords = viz_center + np.array([0, 2, 0]) * 0.5
        point = Dot(point_coords, color=RED, radius=0.1)
        point_lbl = MathTex(r"(1,1)_B = (0,2)_S", color=RED, font_size=20).next_to(point, UR, buff=0.1)
        
        self.play(FadeIn(point), FadeIn(point_lbl))
        
        # Pulse animation to show position invariant property
        self.play(point.animate.scale(2), run_time=0.4, rate_func=there_and_back)
        self.play(point.animate.scale(2), run_time=0.4, rate_func=there_and_back)
        
        self.wait(2)
        self.play(self.lecture[4].animate.set_color(WHITE))

class Section6Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Fetching data from storyboard
        title = "Summary and Visual Wrap-up"
        lecture_lines = [
            "Change of basis alters descriptions, not the physical space.",
            "Matrix operations allow us to switch between viewpoints easily.",
            "The geometry stays fixed while our perspective shifts."
        ]
        
        self.setup_layout(title, lecture_lines)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Lecture: "Change of basis alters descriptions, not the physical space."
        # Visual: Flowchart [v]_B -> [P] -> [v]_Standard in white (#FFFFFF)
        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        v_b = MathTex(r"[\vec{v}]_{\mathcal{B}}", color=WHITE)
        p_mat = MathTex(r"P", color=WHITE)
        v_s = MathTex(r"[\vec{v}]_{\mathcal{S}}", color=WHITE)
        arrow1 = Arrow(start=LEFT, end=RIGHT, color=WHITE, buff=0.1)
        arrow2 = Arrow(start=LEFT, end=RIGHT, color=WHITE, buff=0.1)
        
        flowchart = VGroup(v_b, arrow1, p_mat, arrow2, v_s).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.3)
        self.place_in_area(flowchart, "A2", "C5", scale_factor=0.9)
        
        self.play(Write(flowchart))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Lecture: "Matrix operations allow us to switch between viewpoints easily."
        # Visual: Morph the background grid smoothly from standard to skewed and back.
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Use a small NumberPlane for the demonstration
        plane = NumberPlane(
            x_range=[-2, 2, 1],
            y_range=[-2, 2, 1],
            x_length=3,
            y_length=3,
            background_line_style={"stroke_opacity": 0.4}
        )
        self.place_in_area(plane, "D2", "F5", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        # A static point to show it doesn't move
        point = Dot(plane.c2p(1, 1), color=RED)
        point_label = MathTex(r"\vec{v}", color=RED).next_to(point, UR, buff=0.1)
        
        self.play(Create(plane), Create(point), Write(point_label))
        self.wait(0.5)
        
        # Skew matrix
        matrix = [[1, 1], [0.5, 1]]
        
        # Animate morphing (skewing)
        self.play(
            plane.animate.apply_matrix(matrix),
            run_time=2
        )
        self.wait(1)
        
        # Animate back to standard
        self.play(
            plane.animate.apply_matrix(np.linalg.inv(matrix)),
            run_time=2
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Lecture: "The geometry stays fixed while our perspective shifts."
        # Visual: Fade in the text 'Same Space, Different Perspectives' in light blue (#ADD8E6).
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        summary_text = Text("Same Space, Different Perspectives", font_size=24, color="#ADD8E6")
        self.place_at_grid(summary_text, "E3", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        self.play(FadeIn(summary_text, shift=UP))
        self.wait(3)

outline.topic: The Language of Perspective: Change of Basis
outline.target_audience: University students taking Linear Algebra or Calculus III

sections.title: The Intuition: Different Maps, Same World
sections.content: Introduce the core idea that a point in space is absolute, but its coordinates depend on the 'ruler' (basis) we use. Use a visual metaphor of two observers describing the same object.
sections.example: A cat sits in a room. Alice uses a standard floor tile grid (Standard Basis), while Bob uses a diagonal pattern on a rug (Alternative Basis). To Alice, the cat is at (3, 2). To Bob, using his skewed rug-grid, the cat is at a completely different coordinate, yet the cat hasn't moved.

sections.title: Prerequisite Review: Basis and Coordinates
sections.content: Quickly recap that a basis is a set of linearly independent vectors that 'span' the space. Visually show how any vector is just a 'recipe' of scaling and adding these basis vectors.
sections.example: In the standard basis i (1,0) and j (0,1), the vector (3,2) means '3 steps right, 2 steps up'. Animation shows the arrows stretching and adding head-to-tail.

sections.title: The 'New' Ruler: Defining Basis B
sections.content: Introduce a new coordinate system (Basis B) consisting of vectors u and v. Show them as arrows pointing in non-standard directions. Explain that our goal is to translate between the Standard Basis (E) and Basis B.
sections.example: Let vector u = (1, 1) and v = (-1, 1) in standard coordinates. An animation overlays this new 'skewed' grid on top of the standard grid.

sections.title: The Bridge: The Change of Basis Matrix
sections.content: Explain the 'Transition Matrix' (P). This matrix acts as a translator. If we have coordinates in Bob's system, multiplying them by P gives us the coordinates in Alice's system. Crucial point: The columns of P are simply the new basis vectors written in the old system's language.
sections.example: Matrix P = [[1, -1], [1, 1]]. If Bob says a point is at (1, 1) in his system, we multiply P by [1, 1] to get (0, 2) in Alice's standard system. Animation shows the point landing on the same spot in both grids.

sections.title: The Inverse Operation: Going Backwards
sections.content: Introduce the Inverse Matrix (P⁻¹). If P takes us from Bob to Alice, P⁻¹ takes us from Alice back to Bob. This is vital for computer graphics and physics simulations.
sections.example: A drone (character) is programmed in standard coordinates but needs to navigate using its own internal sensors (rotated basis). The onboard computer uses the Inverse Matrix to convert the world map into its own 'view'.

sections.title: Summary and Visual Wrap-up
sections.content: Summarize the flow: [Vector in B] -> Multiply by P -> [Vector in Standard]. Emphasize that Change of Basis is just a 'linear transformation' that changes our perspective without moving the space itself.
sections.example: Final animation: A rotating camera showing a 3D scene where the grid lines change (Basis change) while the objects (points) remain stationary, highlighting the elegance of coordinate transformation.
